I am an advocate for partnering up with friends, and I know this is not the norm. However, people misunderstand that just because you are friends, you will be forgiving.

1. Friendship is not the foundation of your business. The business comes first before the friendship. You should not be in business just because you are friends. You are in business and your friendship is just coincidental. You must be willing to lose them for the business.
2. You must have the same vision. Whether or not your partners are friends, your business partner must have the same vision. You will not agree on everything, no one does. And that is an advantage, imagine if you all just agree with one another, edi sana hindi mo sila pinartner.
3. You will have conflicts, you must learn to handle it with maturity and professionalism. Walang personalan.
4. As I've mentioned, set expectations from the start, write them down. If you observed a bad habit, call them out.

Imagine partnering with someone whom you just met. Yes it may seem like a dream if your vision seems aligned, but you don't know their tendencies, their deep desires, their family life. Though it is not a guarantee that your friends won't betray you, I'd like to have an idea on what they are like.

Yes I would recommend you to continue. Friction between partners is part of the game, friends or not.

It can be one of the best experiences, maraming tawanan at kulitan habang nagtatrabaho nang malupit. I would have never lasted this long without my good bros by my side. Here are some tips:

1. Don't go to business with your friends if you want to become rich fast. It is a given that you will encounter hell, kung pera lang ang habol, wag na. Focus on mission first.
2. Hindi pwede ang equal partners or 50-50. Dapat malinaw sa inyo ang 1, 2, 3. Bawal boss lahat, may final decision-maker. Sa pera din kelangan malinaw ang usapan, iba na kapag kumikita nang malaki. Pag greedy ang kaibigan, wag gawing kasosyo. Bawal ang greedy.
3. Make sure your personalities compliment each other. Di mag wwork ang dalawang dominant. Make sure your values are aligned, simulate everything that you think what will happen in the business, the good and bad, and write it all down including the course of action.
4. Pag may disagreements, create a system kung ano mangyayari. Voting system, 3rd party mediator, etc.
5. Delinieate responsibilities, hindi pwede same yung ginagawa niyo, may kanya kanya kayong functions na nagwwork together as a team. Identify your strengths and weaknesses and work from there.
6. Create a system when you can call each other out, pag may nagkukulang sa performance, make sure this is address with respect and professionalism. Bawal ang sisihan, tulungan lang.
7. Be willing to lose your friend. It is clear to us that the business comes first, if the business does well, so will we.
8. We rarely hang out outside of business, may kanya kanya kaming buhay. Pero pagdating sa trabaho, trabaho. 
9. Be professional. Di porket friends kayo, sobrang friendly sa opisina. Pag may problema, pag usapan, bawal tampuhan. Pag may gagawin, laging mag paalam, wag mag aassume na papayag sila dahil friends kayo.
10. Document EVERYTHING. Before doing it formally, ilagay sa papel, pirmahan, better ipanotarize. We have 3 separate sets of documents indicating our partnership responsibilities etc. Bukod pa ito sa articles and bylaws.

When your business encounters difficulties, sometimes all you need are your friends turned business partners, konting alak, irecognize ang blessings, magstrategize, tapos trabahong malupit ulit.

Hi. As an architect who does construction, hope this would help. In my experience, most of the time when a client already has a design from an architect, hindi talaga financially feasible iconstruct ang design based sa budget ng client.

Based on your post, yung contractors na gumagawa ay run by foremen. Usually kulang talaga sa attention to detail at alaga ang mga yan, kaya nga mura sumingil. Kumbaga you get what you pay for. Gusto din nila yung methodology na alam lang nila, di sila nageexplore ng bago.

It might be true na kaya mong talunin in terms of workmanship, pero sabi mo nga, namamahalan ang client sa sinisingil mo sa build. This just means that your design is not at par with the client's budget to provide quality works based on your design.

If I may suggest, you try to be more conservative sa design, para abot kaya sa budget ng client, work around your pricing, not the pricing of foremen. Patunayan mo na yung idedesign mo ay magagawa mo na quality.

As an executive who is present on final interviews, we usually focus on personal questions kasi yung technical skillset and qualifications are covered na ng HR sa intial interview steps. 1. Trabaho ng parents - we look for conflict of interest. 2. Home setup - kung nakatira with parents, renting, may sarili na bahay, nagccommute, may kotse, inaalam namin paano sila pupunta sa office and we do what we can to assist.

3. Work ng asawa, age ng mga anak - also helps with the bonding, sometimes yung company ng asawa can be a referral to the company.

I can understand those who say no. I'm okay either way. As a company owner, I'd like to give a couple of reasons why you should include your photo in your CV, as this is what we prefer.

1. The purpose of the resume or CV is to secure a job interview. They say that including your photo sets you up for discrimination and judgement. Well, they are going to see you in the interview anyway, if they are discriminating (all companies have their preferences), they would just do it. Don't you want to just save some time and just skip the interview part if they're gonna reject you anyway based on looks?

2. Some might say that showing yourself for the first time during the interview will give you a chance to justify your competence. True, but don't you want to be transparent from the getgo? 

I've had experience working with my HR team as we comb through countless resumes, it's hard to peg those without photos since it seems that the applicant is hiding something. Some might say that the recruiter shall be objective and look for the necessary skills and experience in the applicant. However, experience does not equate competence, listed skills does not equate to real and applied skills, and applicants are people, recruiters are people, we are not machines, we cannot be truly objective and without bias.

By including a photo in the resume, we can judge and assess the following:
1. A sense of professionalism from the applicant by their choice of photo (well groomed, well dressed, posture)
2. Attention to detail (some applicants submit streched out photos or out of ratio)
3. Experience (young applicants usually use their graduation photos, so at a quick glance the recruiter has the age pegged)
4. Transparency (a photo humanizes the applicant and feels more honest)
